2018_125_091818regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held at 7:00 PM on September 18, 2018 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Contents include recognitions of spring 2018 all-state athletes, an ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the CAFR for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2017, MASB awards to Karl Schmidt, Elizabeth Hammond and Gary Hauff, the July 2018 Treasurer's Report showing total disbursements in the period of $8,697,986.96, eight new teacher contracts, staffing and enrollment reports, and a resolution accepting Mondrian Properties' $1,974,000.00 offer for surplus land on Square Lake Road east of John R Road.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 PM, September 18, 2018, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices are at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
- Twelve spring 2018 all-state athletes presented by Mr. Fulcher, among them Tahra Brodbine, Jenna Doyle, Morgan MacDonald and Sahaja Pinnu.
- Mission Moment: the Technology Resource Center replaced 5,000 iPads at the elementary level over the summer, a project requiring staff to handle almost 15,000 iPads; Troy Center for Transition and GROW students assisted, with Beth Soggs presenting.
- ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2017, recognizing Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services.
- MASB awards: Karl Schmidt, Master Board Member (a minimum of 368 education credits); Elizabeth Hammond, Level One Certification; Gary Hauff, 20 Years of Service.
- Student representatives Lauryn Collins (IA East), Mackenzie Malinowski (Troy College & Career HS), Jenna Doyle (Athens HS) and Erin McManus (Troy HS).

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the August 21, 2018 Special Board Retreat (5:35 p.m. to 7:47 p.m.) and the August 21, 2018 regular meeting (7:54 p.m. to 9:38 p.m.), plus the July 2018 Treasurer's Report. The August meeting adopted 18-070 (consent items), 18-071 (personnel) and 18-072, authorizing a D.M. Burr Facilities Management, Inc. contract addendum reflecting a $12.00 per hour minimum wage for custodians with a base increase not to exceed $364,000.

**Personnel and staffing**
Probationary contracts for Caitlyn St. Onge (ASD, Barnard), Jaclyn Moelich (ASD, Morse), Whitney Bernstein (counselor, IA East), James Morang (.8 English, Athens), Angela Correa (.4 math, Baker), Cortney Walls (7th grade science, Smith), Hilda Zanaliu (.4 ELD, Baker) and Whitney Swichtenberg (kindergarten, Leonard). Jordan Harris reported 65 new TSD teachers, 10 TSD graduates, 33 with education beyond a bachelor's degree, 17 with five or more years of experience (5 of these with 10 or more years) and 192 total years as a group.

**Enrollment**
Mark Dziatczak and Kris Griffor compared September 19, 2017 with September 12, 2018: elementary 5630 to 5569, middle schools 2994 to 3085, high schools 4392 to 4366, total students 13016 to 13020.

**Business - Section 1 property sale**
Resolution accepting Mondrian Properties, L.L.C.'s offer for 5.95 +/- acres plus up to 1.74 +/- acres of detention basin north of Square Lake Road east of John R Road (part of Sidwell 20-01-300-016) and an 11.28 +/- acre conservation parcel (Sidwell 20-01-451-001). Price $1,974,000.00, split $1,574,000.00 for the Premises and $400,000.00 for wetland mitigation credits, plus $40,000.00 per unit above 24 units approved by the City of Troy, with a $25,000.00 earnest money deposit and $150,000.00 seed money to Six Rivers Land Conservancy.

**Other**
Certification of Steve Gottlieb, Gary Hauff, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as MASB 2018 Delegate Assembly delegates for the Fall Conference, November 1-4, 2018, and Dr. Machesky's video report on the oneTROY 2018-19 Welcome Back event at Athens High School on August 21st.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, convened at 7:00 PM on September 18, 2018 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District administration is at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** Spring 2018 all-state athletes recognized by Mr. Fulcher were Angela Anderanin and Sahaja Pinnu (Troy HS girls tennis); Paige Anderson, Lauren Fulcher, Grace Johnson, Hanna Palomino and Megan Worrel (Troy HS girls track); Jenna Doyle (Athens HS girls track); Tahra Brodbine, Lauren Miller and Hailey Stewart (Troy HS girls soccer); and Morgan MacDonald (Troy HS girls lacrosse). The TSD Mission Moment covered the Technology Resource Center's summer work: TRC collected all district-owned iPads and replaced 5,000 iPads at the elementary level, requiring staff to handle almost 15,000 iPads. Beth Soggs presented; certificates went to Troy Center for Transition and GROW volunteers Emily Bernacki, Charley Mapes, Erin O'Donovan, Jared Weinberg, Kendall Weinberg, Phil Chu, Johnathan Kim, Alec Watson and Megan Daley. The Association of School Business Officials International awarded the district its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2017, recognizing Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services; the certificate is signed by ASBO President Charles E. Peterson, Jr. and Executive Director John D. Musso, whose letter is dated September 13, 2018. Michigan Association of School Boards awards went to President Karl Schmidt (Master Board Member Award, requiring a minimum of 368 education credits), Trustee Elizabeth Hammond (Level One Certification, CBA Program) and Secretary Gary Hauff (20 Years of Dedicated Service). Student representatives introduced were Lauryn Collins (International Academy East), Mackenzie Malinowski (Troy College and Career High School), Jenna Doyle (Athens High School, 3rd place 2018 state high jump champion, whose Student Council raised almost $400,000 in three years for charity) and Erin McManus (Troy High School).

**Minutes.** The August 21, 2018 Special Board Retreat opened at 5:35 p.m. with Schmidt, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Philippart present and Miletti absent, plus Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Carrier, Carson, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris and West, and six audience members; topics were the Code of Conduct and class size; adjourned 7:47 p.m. The August 21, 2018 regular meeting opened at 7:54 p.m. with two individuals from Channel 4 News and approximately 20 audience members. Resolution 18-070 (Hauff/Fleming) approved the July 17, 2018 minutes, the June 2018 Treasurer's Report and IA-East Schools of Choice Section 105C for 9th grade for 2019/2020; Yes 6, No 0, Absent Miletti. Resolution 18-071 (Philippart/Gottlieb) approved new hires Takouhy Kinzer, David Anderson, Erin Miller, Nicole Ragnoni, Shelby Henderson, Tess Marshall, Shalyn Fortuna, Christina Connolly, Kathryn Knight, Stephanie Fraga, Justin Tout, Angela Weyland, Brandy Misra, Ewa Dabrowski, Jessica Blumer, Georgina Foakes, Mega Michalczak, Sara Anspach, Andrea Clemmons, Gina Ris, Beth Ann Myers, Sydney Barosko, Jacob Greenwood, Andrea Garavanta, Jacklyn Botsford, Amy Gaylor, Kelsey Drabik, Allison Kramer, Brittney Hopkins, Kaitlyn Pace, Lisa Aude, Rebecca McNally, Kristin Lavoie, Carl Rizzi, Abigail Haelewyn, Kevin White, Karly Campagna, Kathleen Bovee, Stephanie Yetter, Morgan Blain, Liliana Cujar, Ashley Erard, Janine Bonhard, Nicole Gloden, Colleen O'Brien, Michael Krcatovich, Erin Collins, Joel Podzikowski, Jessica Jones, Jennifer Walters, Leslie Papastefanou, John Pryde, Rivka Nemes, Jordan Holsbeke, Erika Berger and Jonathan Genautis; Yes 6, No 0, Absent Miletti, with discussion noting 80% of recommended candidates came from job fairs. Resolution 18-072 (Fleming/Gottlieb) authorized an addendum to the D.M. Burr Facilities Management, Inc. contract reflecting a $12.00 per hour minimum wage for custodians, with the base contract increase not to exceed $364,000 from the General Fund; the tally is recorded as Yes 6, No Hammond, Absent Miletti. The contract ends June 30, 2019 and Mr. West said it goes out for bid again in March 2019. Troy residents Heidi and John Helfen addressed the Board on the culture of sports. Dr. Machesky said the District recommends opening ten (10) SOC spots; Mr. Schmidt noted onboarding for Board candidate Nicole Wilson. Adjourned 9:38 p.m.

**Personnel and staffing.** Probationary 2018-2019 contracts were recommended for Caitlyn St. Onge (1.0 ASD, Barnard), Jaclyn Moelich (1.0 ASD, Morse), Whitney Bernstein (1.0 counselor, IA East), James Morang (.8 English, Athens), Angela Correa (.4 math, Baker), Cortney Walls (1.0 7th grade science, Smith), Hilda Zanaliu (.4 ELD, Baker) and Whitney Swichtenberg (1.0 kindergarten, Leonard); prior employers include Avondale, Plymouth-Canton, Eton Academy, Hazel Park, Birmingham Public Schools and West Bloomfield. Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, reported 65 new TSD teachers, 10 TSD graduates, 33 teachers with education beyond a bachelor's degree, 17 with five or more years of previous experience (5 of these with 10 or more years) and 192 total years of previous experience as a group.

Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak and Kris Griffor presented enrollment for September 19, 2017 versus September 12, 2018: Barnard 502 and 486; Bemis 553 and 538; Costello 362 and 362; Hamilton 518 and 515; Hill 334 and 344; Leonard 422 and 420; Martell 489 and 443; Morse 501 and 499; Schroeder 519 and 528; Troy Union 467 and 479; Wass 425 and 420; Wattles 500 and 495; Early Childhood Niles 38 and 40; elementary total 5630 and 5569. **Business - Section 1 property sale.** A Business Services slide summarizes: purchase price $1,574,000 plus $40,000 per lot over 24 lots; mitigation credits $400,000; total money to district $1,924,000 plus $40,000 per lot over 24 lots; Mondrian land conservancy seed money $150,000; total value of deal $2,124,000 plus $40,000 per lot over 24 lots. The resolution recites an RFP for surplus property in Troy, Oakland County: 5.95 +/- acres plus up to 1.74 +/- acres for a detention pond/basin north of Square Lake Road east of John R Road, part of Sidwell Number 20-01-300-016 (the "Premises"), and the remainder plus 11.28 +/- acres (Sidwell Number 20-01-451-001) as the "Conservation Property." The Offer To Purchase Real Estate came from Mondrian Properties, an assumed name for Mondrian Properties, L.L.C., on behalf of an entity to be formed, at $1,974,000.00 plus $40,000.00 for each additional unit over 24 units approved by the City of Troy, with a $25,000.00 earnest money deposit; the price splits into $1,574,000.00 for the Premises and $400,000.00 for wetland mitigation credits and the Charitable Conservancy Contribution. At closing the purchaser donates $150,000.00 in seed money to Six Rivers Land Conservancy and conveys the Conservation Property to it. Terms include a First American Title Insurance Company commitment, a survey within ninety days, a ninety-day inspection period and one 275-day extension period requiring an additional $25,000.00 payment. The seller must obtain City of Troy consent to split the Premises from the approximately 70.647 +/- acre parent parcel supporting a site plan of 24 lots; the price assumes approval for a minimum of seventeen (17) lots/units. The purchaser must apply to the City of Troy and the MDEQ within thirty days, negotiate a Conservation Easement with MDEQ and an endowment agreement with Six Rivers Land Conservancy including at least $150,000.00 seed money, and close within thirty days at Clark Hill PLC. Seller's consultant is Bill Bowman of Great Northern Consulting Group, (586) 703-9882. Notices go to Mondrian Properties, L.L.C., 50215 Schoenherr Road, Shelby Township, Michigan 48315, Attn: Joseph Maniaci, with a copy to Lawrence M. Dudek of Miller Canfield Paddock and Stone, P.L.C., 150 W. Jefferson, Suite 2500, Detroit; and to Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Attn. Rick West, with a copy to Dana L. Abrahams, Clark Hill PLC, 151 S. Old Woodward, Suite 200, Birmingham, MI 48009. Michigan law governs with venue in Oakland County; seller representations survive closing six months. The offer is signed by Joseph Maniaci, Manager, and Superintendent Richard Machesky. Exhibits include the legal description, a warranty deed citing Section 108 of the Michigan Land Division Act (Act No. 288, Public Acts of 1967) with transfer tax exempt under MCLA 207.505(h)(i) and 207.526(h)(i), an Agreement for Conservation Easement, a release and hold harmless, and the concept plan. The certification cites the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Other.** The Board was to certify Steve Gottlieb, Gary Hauff, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2018 Delegate Assembly during the MASB Fall Conference, November 1-4, 2018, certified by Secretary Gary N. Hauff. Dr. Machesky was to report on and share the video from the oneTROY 2018-19 Welcome Back event held for all TSD staff at Athens High School on August 21st.
